hero.title: Every replay you have played, read together
hero.tagline: Blueberry Academy imports your Pokémon Showdown replays and says what your teams and your brings actually did — by game, by series, with the sample size next to every number.

problem.title: Showdown keeps the replays. It does not answer the question.
problem.body: A ladder run is hundreds of games, each behind its own link and each shown one at a time. Which of your teams is actually winning, which four you brought into what, whether this month is better than last — none of that is anywhere, and counting it by hand is why nobody does.

import.title: Import in one go
import.body: Paste replay links, or sync every public replay a Showdown name has played. Battles already imported are skipped before they are fetched, so a sync that stopped picks up where it left off.

teams.title: Teams, and the four you brought
teams.body: Games are grouped by the six you registered and by the four that actually appeared — those are different questions — and ranked by Wilson lower bound, so three wins from three games does not top the table. Every group carries its sample size.

timeline.title: Read a game back
timeline.body: Open any game and its turns are flattened into a list: moves, switches, terastallisation, what was standing on the field. In English or 繁體中文, names included.

start.title: Getting started
start.one: Sign in with Google. There is no password to set and none to forget.
start.two: Add the Showdown names you play under. That is what decides which side of a battle is you.
start.three: Paste a few replay links, or sync a whole account and leave it running.
start.note: Showdown gives no other site a way to verify that an account is yours, so those names grant nothing: they only decide which of the battles you imported count as your own.
start.cta: Sign in and import your first replay

about.title: About
about.lede: Blueberry Academy reads the replays you have already played and counts them. This page says what it reads, how it counts, and what it leaves out — so that a win rate on the dashboard can be read for what it is.

source.title: What it reads
source.body: One Showdown replay is one game. The raw log is fetched from replay.pokemonshowdown.com and stored exactly as it arrived; everything else — the format, the result, the six registered at team preview, the four that appeared — is derived from it. Nothing is typed in, and the log stays the only source of truth: when the parser learns to read more of a log, the derived data is rebuilt from the copy already stored rather than fetched again.

counting.title: What a number counts
counting.unit: Every game is stored on its own, including the games of a best-of-three series — a series result can be derived from its games, and not the other way round. Which unit a number is counted in follows from the format you filter to: a ladder format is counted per game, a best-of-three format per series.
counting.format: A ladder format and its best-of-three counterpart are separate items and are never averaged together. Showdown treats them as different formats, and they are played differently enough that one number over both would describe neither.
counting.spectated: A battle where neither player is on your list of Showdown names is a spectated battle. It is stored and it can be read, and it counts towards none of your statistics. Binding the name you played under claims it; removing that name hands it back.

teams.title: Teams and brings
teams.team: A team is the six revealed at team preview. Two battles are the same team when both the six and the format are the same. Items and moves are no part of that: a ladder replay does not carry them, and requiring them would leave almost every battle alone in a group of one.
teams.bring: A bring is the four that actually appeared, which is not always the four that were picked — a game that ends early can leave the fourth never having shown up, and that is common rather than exceptional. Those games count for the team and for none of the brings, and the team page says how many they were instead of leaving the difference to look like an arithmetic error.

ranking.title: How teams are ranked
ranking.body: By the lower bound of a Wilson score interval rather than by win rate: three wins from three games is a 100% win rate, and it belongs below a season played at 70%. Every group carries its sample size, and no group is hidden for being small — a rate counted from five games is worth seeing, as long as it says it came from five.

limits.title: What it does not do
limits.body: It says what happened, not why. It offers no advice on what to play, ranks you against nobody, and cannot verify that a Showdown account is yours — nobody can, and what that means for your data is on the next page.

about.privacy: What is kept, and what cannot be verified

privacy.title: Privacy and terms
privacy.lede: This is a personal project that keeps other people's replays and the Showdown names you say are yours. This page says what is kept, who can read it, what cannot be checked, and how to have it removed.

stored.title: What is kept
stored.account: An account, created when you sign in with Google: the email address and account id Google returns. There is no password, and none is stored.
stored.names: The Showdown names you add. Kept as you typed them, compared with case and punctuation removed.
stored.battles: One row per replay you import, holding what was derived from it — the format, when it was played, the result, the ratings, the two signatures, the turn count — and a record of both sides of the battle: the opponent's name, their six, and what appeared.
stored.logs: The raw log of every replay you import, gzipped and untouched, in a private bucket under a path that begins with your account id.

access.title: Who can read it
access.body: You. Rows are scoped to your account id by the database itself rather than by the app asking nicely, and the bucket holding the logs is private and split by the same id. Nothing on this site is published: there is no profile page, no shared link, no leaderboard, and no page that shows one person's battles to another.

unverified.title: What cannot be verified
unverified.body: That a Showdown account is yours. Showdown offers other sites no way to check it — there is no sign-in to use and no field on a Showdown profile to put a code in — so adding a name is trust and nothing else. The same name may be on more than one person's list, and a name on your list grants nothing beyond deciding which of the battles you imported are treated as your own.
unverified.public: The replays themselves are public on Showdown to begin with, and both players' names and teams are in the log at its public address. Importing one copies that public record into your account; it does not make anything visible that was not already.

unbinding.title: What removing a name does
unbinding.body: Attribution is that list of names re-derived, so removing one takes every battle under it back to being a spectated battle: out of every statistic, off the dashboard, still stored. Nothing is deleted, and binding the name again brings those battles back exactly as they were.

deletion.title: Deleting your data
deletion.body: There is no delete button yet — this is the honest answer rather than a policy. Signing out ends the session and removes nothing. To have the account, its rows and its stored logs deleted, ask through the project's repository, and it will be done by hand.

others.title: Who else your browser talks to
others.body: Google, when you sign in. Supabase, which holds the database, the logs and your session. Cloudflare, which serves this site. Pokémon Showdown, when an import fetches a replay and when a page draws Pokémon icons, which are loaded from Showdown's own sprite sheet rather than copied here.
others.browser: There is no analytics, no advertising and no tracking of any kind. What is kept in your browser is the sign-in session, and which theme and language you chose.

terms.title: Terms
terms.body: This is offered as is, with no warranty and no promise that it will keep running, keep your data, or be correct. It is not a backup: the replays it reads are Showdown's, at their own public addresses.
terms.trademarks: Not affiliated with Nintendo, Creatures, GAME FREAK, The Pokémon Company, Smogon or Pokémon Showdown. Pokémon names and sprites belong to their owners; replays belong to the people who played them.

notFound.title: There is nothing at this address
notFound.body: The link may be an old one, or the address may have a typo in it. Everything else is still here.

unexpected.title: Something went wrong here
unexpected.body: This page could not be shown. Loading it again is often enough; if it is not, nothing you have imported is affected.

login.title: Sign in
login.tagline: Google only — there is no password to forget.
login.failed: That sign-in did not go through.

import.title: Import a replay
import.tagline: Paste replay links, or sync everything a Showdown account has played.

paste.title: Paste links
paste.tagline: One replay per line. A private replay keeps its password in the address, so paste the whole thing.

import.label: Replay links, one per line

sync.title: Sync an account
sync.tagline: Every public replay Showdown will admit to for this name. Battles already imported are skipped before they are even fetched, so pressing this again after a stopped import picks up where it left off.
sync.label: Showdown name
sync.unusable: That is not a Showdown name — it needs at least one letter or digit.
sync.truncated: Showdown ran out of search pages before this account ran out of replays, so this is not the whole history. A single search reaches about 5000 replays; the rest need a narrower search.

import.profileFailed: We could not read your Showdown names, so nothing can be imported right now — without them there is no way to tell which side of a battle is yours. Reload the page to try again.

progress.label: Import progress
progress.listing: Asking Showdown what this account has played…

import.badLink: That is not a Showdown replay link. Paste the address of the replay itself, like https://replay.pokemonshowdown.com/gen9championsvgc2026regmb-2667169457 — a private replay keeps its password in the address, so paste that too.
import.unparsed: The raw log is stored, but this replay could not be read: {message} Nothing is lost — the battle is kept and can be read again once the parser understands that log.

status.unparsedShort: stored, but the log could not be read

import.allSpectated: Every battle that came in was filed as one you only watched: no player in any of them is on your list of Showdown names, so none of them counts towards your statistics and none of them will reach your dashboard. Add the name you played under and they are claimed the moment you do — the replays are already here and nothing needs importing again.

failed.notFound: Showdown has no replay at that link. It may have been deleted, or it may be private — a private replay is only served with the password its address carries.
failed.unavailable: Showdown did not answer. It may be down or rate limiting; wait a moment and import the link again.
failed.malformed: Showdown answered with something that is not a replay. Nothing was stored.
failed.storeFailed: The raw log could not be stored, so no battle was recorded. Nothing is half-imported — try the link again.
failed.writeFailed: The raw log was stored, but the battle could not be written to your records. Import the link again.

battle.spectated: Neither player is on your list of Showdown names, so this battle is stored but counts towards none of your statistics, and it will not reach your dashboard. Add the name you played under and it is claimed the moment you do — the replay is already here and nothing needs importing again.

aliases.title: Showdown names
aliases.tagline: Add every name you play under and they all count as the same you — after a rename, on an alt, on a separate account for a different format.
aliases.unverified: We cannot verify that a Showdown account is yours, and neither can anyone else: Showdown has no way for another site to check. These names only decide which of the battles you import are treated as your own — they grant nothing, and the same name may be on more than one person’s list.
aliases.label: Showdown name
aliases.empty: No names yet. Add the one you play under.
aliases.alreadyBound: {name} is already on your list. Names are compared without case or punctuation, so NotLittleStar and notlittlestar are the same name.
aliases.unusable: That is not a Showdown name — it needs at least one letter or digit.
aliases.loadFailed: We could not read your names, so nothing can be changed here right now. Reload the page to try again.
aliases.reattributeHint: Runs the names above over every battle you have imported. Nothing to undo — a run that changes nothing writes nothing.
aliases.removeBody: This takes {count} battle out of your statistics. It goes back to being a spectated battle, and binding the name again brings it back exactly as it was. | This takes {count} battles out of your statistics. They go back to being spectated battles, and binding the name again brings them back exactly as they were.
aliases.removeBodyUnknown: This takes every battle under that name out of your statistics. They go back to being spectated battles, and binding the name again brings them back exactly as they were.
aliases.unbound: Done: {count} battle went back to spectated. | Done: {count} battles went back to spectated.
aliases.reattributedWithReturned: Done: {attributed} battles are now yours, {reattributed} were turned over to a different name, and {unattributed} went back to spectated.
aliases.reattributed: Done: {attributed} battles are now yours, and {reattributed} were turned over to a different name.
aliases.reattributionFailed: That did not finish. {processed} battles were worked through before it stopped; nothing was undone, and running it again picks up the rest.

teams.noBrings: No game with this team has a complete bring yet.
teams.unfiled: These ended before every pick had appeared, so no complete bring covers them. They count for the team and in none of the brings.
teams.notFound: No team here. It may have dropped out of the current filters.

teams.empty: No battles match these filters yet.
teams.emptyUnbound: None of the battles here are yours yet, and importing more will not change that: which side of a battle is you is decided by the Showdown names on your profile, and there are none on it — so every replay you import is filed as one you only watched. Bind the name you play under first. The battles already imported under it are claimed at the same moment, so nothing needs importing again.
teams.ranking: Wilson lower bound {score}% — the sort key

trend.title: Recent form
trend.noRating: None of these battles carried a ladder rating. A best-of series is not played on the ladder, so there is no number to plot.
trend.descriptive: This says what happened, not why.
trend.gap: The x axis is the calendar, so two months without a game take up two months of width and the win rate curve stretches flat across the break rather than hiding it. The rating line does not stretch: it stops at the last battle that carried a rating and starts again at the next one that did, because a best-of series is not played on the ladder and there is no number in between. Each point of the win rate curve covers the games leading up to that day, so the first points of a curve cover fewer games than the window says.
